events.credibility_reason: README reports no output and no dates; the 10^30 figure attributed to it is unconfirmed and conflicts with OEIS usage.

why: The statement asks only whether a friend of 10 exists; no event decides it. The close call is whether necessary conditions on a hypothetical friend (prime-factor counts, prime-divisor bounds, size and exponent bounds) are `bound` or `none`. I read them as `bound`: they move quantities that constrain the minimal possible counterexample (number of distinct primes, sizes of prime divisors), analogous to lower bounds for odd perfect numbers, and leave the question open. Journal publication (Indagationes, Resonance, Oradea, Calcutta Math. Soc.) counts as digested; the Pith AI review of 2412.02701 does not count either way. Ward and Chatterjee–Mandal–Mandal have no journal of record in the record, so unreviewed. Cemra is a finite search (instances); the 14 and 20 papers are different numbers (variant). No AI system produced any mathematics: the only AI engagement is automated reviews/summaries.
doubts: Scope for the restriction papers could defensibly be `none` (the statement is yes/no and they settle no quantity it names); this would change the problem from progress to open. Refereeing of the Calcutta Math. Soc. bulletin is unverified. AlphaProof Nexus's 44 OEIS conjectures were not checked for relevance.
